---
title: "Reproduce the published evidence"
description: "Exact runtime, inputs, checksums, SCOP-native figure provenance, manifests, checkpoints, rebuild commands, deterministic boundaries, and verification gates for SCOP Learn."
---

The website is a rendered view of an evidence chain. The source data or bundled object produces a checkpoint and complete result; SCOP produces the published analysis plot; component manifests record execution states and hashes; a top-level manifest binds all committed evidence together.

::: {.learning-objectives}
## Learning outcomes

You will learn to:

1. rebuild all committed real-data evidence from the named inputs;
2. verify component and figure hashes instead of trusting file names;
3. distinguish deterministic code, environment-dependent output, and unavailable backends;
4. confirm that every published analysis PNG comes from an exported SCOP plotter;
5. adapt the evidence-chain pattern to your own study.
:::

## 1 · Audited runtime

| Component | Published value |
|---|---|
| R | 4.5.1 |
| SCOP | 0.8.9 |
| Seurat | 5.5.0 |
| seed | `20260807` |
| SCOP namespace exports | 314 |

The generated [runtime manifest](evidence/real-data/runtime.json) also records optional backend availability:

| Backend/package | Evidence runtime |
|---|---|
| CellTypist | available and executed |
| edgeR | available and executed |
| harmony | available and executed |
| clustree | available and executed |
| SingleR / celldex | unavailable; not executed |
| spacexr | unavailable; RCTD not executed |
| zellkonverter | unavailable; H5AD conversion not executed |
| loomR | unavailable; Loom conversion not executed |

Package startup warnings that a dependency was built under a nearby R patch version do not automatically invalidate a result, but they belong in the session record and should be investigated if numerical or ABI failures occur.

## 2 · Source input and checksum

Five teaching objects come from the installed SCOP package. The external raw-format case uses the official 10x PBMC 1k v3 filtered H5:

```text
SHA-256  8191f576550c1b449d03441b9eb098ee9f73fa82513d171ba87d31d551e3ffda
features 33,538
cells    1,222
UMIs     9,235,144
```

Download it into the ignored artifact directory:

```bash
mkdir -p artifacts/real-data/input
curl -L --fail \
  -o artifacts/real-data/input/pbmc_1k_v3_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5 \
  https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-exp/3.0.0/pbmc_1k_v3/pbmc_1k_v3_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5
```

Verify before running R:

```bash
shasum -a 256 artifacts/real-data/input/pbmc_1k_v3_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5
```

If the checksum differs, stop. Do not silently update the expected value; determine whether the source changed, the download is incomplete, or the wrong file was used.

::: {.input-contract}
**Rebuild contract**

- repository checked out at a named commit;
- expected H5 checksum matches;
- installed R/SCOP/Seurat versions recorded;
- write access to ignored `artifacts/`;
- sufficient memory/disk for 163 MB cross-source checkpoint and temporary matrices;
- optional backend status captured before interpreting module failures.
:::

## 3 · Run the evidence builder

From the repository root:

```bash
Rscript scripts/build-real-evidence.R
```

The script executes seven stages:

1. runtime/package/backend inventory;
2. 10x H5 → three-file → RDS structural round-trip;
3. real `pancreas_sub` single-sample construction;
4. real `panc8_sub` SCT + Harmony integration;
5. real `pbmcmultiome_sub` annotation evaluation and panc8 pseudobulk;
6. real human/mouse Visium spatial workflows;
7. component hashes, figure provenance, critical assertions, and session record.

Successful completion prints seven component manifests and eleven real-data figures. It also stops if a critical assertion fails.

### Ignored but hashed checkpoints

Large RDS files are written under `artifacts/real-data/checkpoints/`. They are not committed, but their path, byte size, and SHA-256 appear in component manifests. This lets a local rebuild prove which object generated a result without putting large binaries in Git.

## 5 · Verify the top-level manifest

The manifest contains seven component records, eleven figure records, and critical assertions. Every figure record includes `path`, `sha256`, `bytes`, `plot_function`, `dataset`, and `source_checkpoint`.

```r
manifest <- jsonlite::read_json(
  "evidence/real-data/manifest.json",
  simplifyVector = TRUE
)

stopifnot(length(manifest$components) == 7)
stopifnot(length(manifest$figures) == 11)
stopifnot(all(unlist(manifest$critical_assertions)))

plot_functions <- vapply(manifest$figures, `[[`, character(1), "plot_function")
stopifnot(all(vapply(strsplit(plot_functions, " + ", fixed = TRUE), function(x) {
  all(startsWith(x, "scop::"))
}, logical(1))))
```

Hash verification:

```r
sha256 <- function(path) {
  digest::digest(path, algo = "sha256", file = TRUE)
}

for (item in manifest$components) {
  stopifnot(file.exists(item$path), identical(sha256(item$path), item$sha256))
}
for (item in manifest$figures) {
  stopifnot(file.exists(item$path), identical(sha256(item$path), item$sha256))
}
```

If `digest` is unavailable, use `openssl::sha256(file(path))` or the system `shasum -a 256`, then compare the hexadecimal value. Do not weaken the check to file existence.

## 6 · Published figure provenance

Every analysis PNG in the current manifest is drawn by an exported SCOP plotter:

| Figure family | SCOP plotter |
|---|---|
| single-sample QC | `FeatureStatPlot()` |
| cluster stability | `ClusterTreePlot()` |
| dimension evidence | `DimsEstimatePlot()` |
| single/cross-source embedding | `CellDimPlot()` |
| annotation markers | `GroupHeatmap()` |
| pseudobulk differential expression | `VolcanoPlot()` |
| spatial domains/features | `SpatialSpotPlot()` + `SpatialVariableFeaturePlot()` |
| spatial graph | `SpatialNetworkPlot()` |
| spatial neighbourhoods | `SpatialNeighborhoodPlot()` |

External modelling is allowed when SCOP is not the statistical engine—for example, edgeR produces the valid pseudobulk table—but the displayed analysis plot and its function provenance remain explicit.

## 7 · Critical assertions and exact outcomes

The build must prove:

- H5 ↔ three-file dimensions and total UMI equality;
- H5 ↔ RDS dimensions;
- 979 cells retained in the executed single-sample case;
- a real Harmony reduction in the cross-source case;
- non-empty pseudobulk results: 16 pseudo-samples, 5,227 genes tested, 527 meeting the stated threshold;
- at least 20 Moran-ranked spatial features;
- all analysis figures use SCOP plotters;
- no synthetic dataset is primary evidence.

These numbers are regression expectations for the locked runtime/data, not universal biological thresholds.

## 8 · Render the bilingual website

After evidence succeeds:

```bash
quarto render
```

The GitHub quality workflow uses Quarto 1.10.18 and verifies:

- all English/Chinese routes exist and have parity;
- metadata, canonical and language-alternate links;
- no local paths or token patterns leak into output;
- all internal links/anchors and image alt text;
- component/figure hashes and execution states;
- external HTTPS links;
- browser accessibility for English and Chinese home pages.

If local Quarto is unavailable, CI can render, but local source-level and figure-level verification should still run before publication.

## 9 · Deterministic, environment-dependent, and external components

| Component | Reproducibility expectation |
|---|---|
| source checksum, dimensions, total counts | exact |
| manifest/component hashes on same locked output | exact |
| filtering rules and retained cell identities | exact under locked input/runtime |
| edgeR result table | expected exact/near-exact under locked versions |
| clustering/UMAP coordinates | seed-controlled but may vary across numerical libraries/platforms |
| CellTypist | depends on Python environment and exact model file |
| optional databases (motifs, pathways, references) | must be versioned separately |
| H5AD/Loom/RCTD in this runtime | not executed, so no output reproducibility claim |

A seed controls stochastic calls that honor it. It does not freeze external models, databases, C++ math libraries, or a package resolver.

## 10 · Clean-room verification strategy

For a serious release:

1. clone into a new directory;
2. verify the commit and source H5 checksum;
3. create a clean R library/environment;
4. install the locked package versions;
5. rebuild evidence once;
6. compare manifests, numeric invariants, and every PNG visually;
7. render the site;
8. inspect desktop and mobile pages;
9. preserve the build log and new manifest as release evidence.

Do not delete a previous known-good manifest until the new build has passed. A rollback requires a known-good commit and evidence bundle.

::: {.checkpoint}
**Reproduction checkpoint**

A rebuild is accepted only when the input checksum matches, all critical assertions are true, component and figure hashes validate, eleven analysis figures have SCOP-native provenance, the bilingual site renders, and the actual exported images—not only the plotting code—have been visually inspected.
:::

## Failure modes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Response |
|---|---|---|
| H5 hash mismatch | wrong/partial/updated file | stop and resolve source identity |
| checkpoint hash differs but numeric assertions pass | serialization/platform difference | compare versions, object invariants, and result tables; document difference |
| UMAP differs slightly | platform/numerical dependency | compare neighbourhood metrics and biological structure |
| CellTypist label set changes | model/environment drift | lock model file/version and rerun annotation review |
| manifest says `not executed` | optional backend absent | install/validate explicitly or keep the honest boundary |
| figure exists but provenance missing | unmanaged/manual plotting path | regenerate through registered SCOP plotter |

::: {.exercise}
## Practice task

Create a mini-manifest for one of your figures containing input checksum, object checkpoint hash, result-table hash, plot function, exact arguments, dataset/sample design, runtime versions, figure hash, and allowed claim. Then delete the figure and prove it regenerates from the recorded checkpoint.
:::

::: {.boundary}
Reproducibility proves that a defined computation can be regenerated. It does not prove that the scientific design is unbiased, the cohort is representative, the labels are true, or the biological interpretation is causal.
:::
